review.notes: Reviewed for age appropriateness, language clarity, and pathway balance across Grades 6-8.

items.prompt: I enjoy reading stories and expressing my ideas through writing.
I like solving number puzzles and figuring out how things work step-by-step.
I understand new concepts easily when I see diagrams, maps, and illustrations.
I often remember facts better when they are set to a rhythm, tune, or song.
I learn best when doing hands-on experiments or building physical models.
I enjoy observing plants, animals, and patterns in the natural environment.
When your class starts a topic about the solar system, how would you most like to explore it?

options.label: Read an illustrated article explaining each planet's atmosphere
Compare distances, orbital speeds, and temperatures in a data table
Study an animated 3D visual map of planetary orbits
Listen to a catchy mnemonic song naming the planets in order

items.prompt: Your teacher asks you to explain the water cycle to younger students. What activity would you choose?

options.label: Act out evaporation, condensation, and rain using gestures and movement
Take the students outside to examine morning dew and cloud formations
Write a narrative story about a raindrop's journey from ocean to cloud
Draw a flowchart tracing the cycle with temperature changes and arrows

items.prompt: To prepare for a science exhibition on renewable energy, which project would you pick?

options.label: Create a detailed visual infographic showing solar panel and wind turbine designs
Compose an energetic audio podcast with rhythmic sound effects
Build a working cardboard windmill model with rotating blades
Survey local weather conditions and record sunlight and wind patterns over a week

items.prompt: When studying how ancient civilizations traded goods, what method helps you understand it best?

options.label: Analyze historical trade routes on an ancient geographic map
Read journal excerpts written by ancient travelers and merchants
Calculate exchange rates and coin valuations in trade transactions
Participate in a hands-on classroom marketplace simulation trading replica goods

items.prompt: If you are learning about bird migration, which resource would you find most interesting?

options.label: Listen to audio recordings comparing different bird calls and flock signals
Track seasonal arrival times of migratory species in a nearby wetland
Calculate travel distances and flight speeds using wing-span formulas
Study color-coded flight corridors and altitude maps across continents

items.prompt: During a history lesson on how message communication evolved, how would you engage?

options.label: Write a comparative essay analyzing letters versus telegrams
Practice tapping out Morse code rhythms using sound beats
Assemble and test a string-telephone acoustic demonstration
Examine how carrier pigeons used magnetic fields and landmarks in nature to navigate

items.prompt: When studying simple machines like levers and pulleys, what helps you grasp the concept?

options.label: Derive the mechanical advantage formula: force times distance
Observe how bird beaks and animal jaws work as levers in nature
Read historical accounts of how ancient builders used inclined planes
Examine cross-section blueprints and vector diagrams of pulley systems

items.prompt: To learn the periodic table and chemical elements, which technique appeals to you?

options.label: Memorize the elements with a rhyming song that matches atomic numbers
Handle element samples and sort physical element cards by weight
Analyze patterns in atomic weights and electron configurations
Study a colorful color-coded poster grouping metals, non-metals, and gases

items.prompt: When studying how plants adapt to harsh climates, which study approach do you prefer?

options.label: Collect leaf and bark specimens to classify moisture-retention features
Read descriptive field notes written by botanists exploring arid regions
Perform a lab experiment comparing water loss across waxed and non-waxed paper leaves
Listen to an audio documentary with ambient desert sounds and expert commentary

items.prompt: Your class is studying ocean currents. How would you prefer to explore this topic?

options.label: View animated satellite maps showing warm and cold ocean streams
Solve equations relating water density, salinity, and temperature
Investigate how marine species use current pathways for seasonal migration
Read an adventure story of sailors navigating the Gulf Stream

items.prompt: When discovering how sound waves travel through different materials, what would you do first?

options.label: Play different musical instruments and compare their pitch and resonance
Touch a vibrating tuning fork placed against water and solid blocks
Calculate wave frequency and wavelength using speed-of-sound formulas
Look at oscilloscope diagrams illustrating crests, troughs, and amplitude

items.prompt: In an ecology unit on food webs, how would you demonstrate how energy moves?

options.label: Write a descriptive guide introducing producers, herbivores, and apex predators
Listen to a rhythmic spoken-word poem highlighting energy transfer across trophic levels
Construct a food web with yarn and cards connecting classmates in a web activity
Observe and document predator-prey relationships in a school garden ecosystem
